Let's confirm the ConfigMap content and check deployment history/events to establish exactly what changed and when.

Strong finding: the Deployment's live spec confirms **revision 2** was triggered by a `kubectl rollout restart` (`kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt: 2026-10-02T11:00:12-04:00` = 15:00:12 UTC) — only 9 seconds after the namespace was created (15:00:03Z). The old pod (revision 1, ReplicaSet `frontend-76d98597b9`) is still logging healthy `200 OK` responses as of 15:02:34 — it started before/at the point the ConfigMap had bad content and its already-running nginx master process never reparsed the file. The new pod (revision 2, ReplicaSet `frontend-d6db5d589`) started fresh after the restart, read the current (broken) ConfigMap, and nginx failed its startup config validation. This explains both the crash loop AND why 2/2 old pods are still serving traffic fine — it's a stuck rolling update, not a full outage.

Let me check incident/blast-radius context to complete the picture.

## Root Cause: CONFIRMED

**Symptom actively occurring:** `kubectl get pods -n shop` shows `frontend-d6db5d589-dn4kr` in `CrashLoopBackOff`, Restart Count 3, Last State `Terminated/Error/Exit Code 1` (as of investigation time).

**Mechanism (direct evidence):**
```
kubectl logs frontend-d6db5d589-dn4kr -n shop --previous
2026/10/02 15:01:36 [emerg] 1#1: unknown directive "proxy_conect_timeout" in /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:9
nginx: [emerg] unknown directive "proxy_conect_timeout" in /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:9
```
The ConfigMap `frontend-nginx` (mounted at `/etc/nginx/conf.d`) contains a typo: `proxy_conect_timeout` instead of `proxy_connect_timeout`. This is baked into the ConfigMap's `last-applied-configuration` annotation, i.e., it was applied deliberately via `kubectl apply`, not a stray live edit. nginx validates its *entire* config at every container start and refuses to boot on an unknown directive — exit 1, repeat → CrashLoopBackOff.

**Why only the new pod crashes, not all of them:** The Deployment's live spec shows `kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt: 2026-10-02T11:00:12-04:00` (15:00:12 UTC) on the pod template — a `kubectl rollout restart` was issued just 9 seconds after the ConfigMap/Deployment were created (15:00:03Z), spawning new ReplicaSet `frontend-d6db5d589`. The two pods in the old ReplicaSet `frontend-76d98597b9` were already running (and had already loaded the config into the nginx master process in memory) and continued serving traffic fine — confirmed by their access logs showing continuous `200 OK` responses through 15:02:34, well after the bad pod started crashing. New pods created *after* the ConfigMap went bad fail immediately on startup; already-running nginx processes don't reparse config without a reload.

**Timing match:** ConfigMap/typo exists now (`resourceVersion 13224`, newer than the Deployment's own `13235`); rollout-restart annotation timestamp (15:00:12) lines up exactly with the new pod's creation and first crash at 15:00:53/15:01:36.

**Current blast radius:** Deployment shows `READY 2/2`, `AVAILABLE 2`, `UP-TO-DATE 1/2` — the two old pods are still healthy and serving all traffic. **This is a stuck rolling update, not a user-facing outage.** `get_incident`/`service_impact` show no correlated alerts or downstream dependents affected.

## Self-check
1. Alternative ruled out: not an OOM (no OOMKilled events, memory limit 64Mi not hit), not an image pull issue (image already present, pulled successfully 4x), not a readiness-probe-only issue (probe fails *because* the process never starts — container never binds to port 80).
2. Direct evidence of the reported symptom: `CrashLoopBackOff` state + exit code 1 + the exact nginx `[emerg]` parse error at container startup — this is the primary mechanism, not inferred.
3. Timing explained: config became invalid, then `rollout restart` created a fresh pod against the already-bad config at the exact timestamp matching first crash.

## Remediation Validation

```text
VALIDATED FIXES:
1. FIX CONFIGMAP TYPO: kubectl patch configmap frontend-nginx -n shop --type merge -p \
   '{"data":{"default.conf":"upstream api {\n    server api:8080;\n}\nserver {\n    listen 80;\n    location /healthz { return 200 \"ok\\n\"; }\n    location /api/ {\n        proxy_pass http://api/;\n        proxy_connect_timeout 2s;\n    }\n    location / { return 200 \"shop frontend\\n\"; }\n}\n"}}'
   Validated by: `kubectl get configmap frontend-nginx -n shop -o yaml` → confirmed exact broken line 9 is
   "proxy_conect_timeout 2s;" inside the /api/ location block; corrected directive is "proxy_connect_timeout 2s;".
   Risk: low | Undo: kubectl patch configmap frontend-nginx -n shop --type merge -p '{"data":{"default.conf":"<prior content>"}}'
   Note: BLOCKED under current READ-ONLY/ASK policy (mutating kubectl denied). Requires an engineer with write access.
   Effect once applied: kubelet syncs the ConfigMap volume to the pod (~60s), and kubelet's existing CrashLoopBackOff
   restart cycle on frontend-d6db5d589-dn4kr will pick up the corrected config on its next retry — no further action needed.

2. ROLLBACK (NOT RECOMMENDED): kubectl rollout undo deployment/frontend -n shop
   Validated by: `kubectl get replicaset -n shop -l app=frontend` → confirmed revision-1 ReplicaSet
   frontend-76d98597b9 (2/2 ready) still exists, so a rollback target technically exists.
   Rejected because: the Deployment's pod template references the ConfigMap by name only — rolling back the
   Deployment revision does NOT revert the ConfigMap's data. The broken ConfigMap would persist and any future
   pod restart/reschedule of the "healthy" old pods would hit the same crash. This does not address root cause.
```

**Recommended action:** Fix #1 only — correct the ConfigMap directive typo. This is the sole fix in the causal chain.

streamingThoughts.content: I'll start with history to see if this matches a known pattern, then verify with fresh evidence from the live cluster.

Found one open incident matching this exact alert (likely this one). Prior frontend history is about a different alert type (KubeDeploymentRolloutStuck from image tag typo) — not CrashLooping. That's a different mechanism; I will not assume it applies here. Let's get fresh evidence from the live cluster.

Hypothesis: pod crash looping could be OOM (like worker's past issue), bad config/env change, or probe failure. Testing by checking current pod status first.

New ReplicaSet frontend-d6db5d589 has one pod crash looping (3 restarts in 71s) while old ReplicaSet pods run fine. This is an active rollout due to a config change. Let's inspect the crashing pod's logs, events, and the new ReplicaSet's config to find what changed.

Confirmed: nginx fails to start with nginx: [emerg] unknown directive "proxy_conect_timeout" in /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:9 — a config syntax error (typo: missing "n" in "connect"). This is the root cause: a ConfigMap-sourced nginx config change introduced a syntax error. The old ReplicaSet's pods are untouched/already-running so they don't re-parse the config, but any new pod reading the current ConfigMap fails immediately. Let's confirm the ConfigMap content and check deployment history/events to establish exactly what changed and when.

The ConfigMap frontend-nginx currently contains the typo proxy_conect_timeout (should be proxy_connect_timeout), matching the last-applied-configuration annotation — meaning it was applied via kubectl apply, not a live edit, and is baked into the ConfigMap's desired state. rollout history is blocked by policy (mutating-kubectl denylist). Let me verify whether the old (healthy) ReplicaSet's pods also hit this nginx config error at their own startup — this will tell us whether the ConfigMap already had the typo when they started.

Strong finding: the Deployment's live spec confirms revision 2 was triggered by a kubectl rollout restart (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt: 2026-10-02T11:00:12-04:00 = 15:00:12 UTC) — only 9 seconds after the namespace was created (15:00:03Z). The old pod (revision 1, ReplicaSet frontend-76d98597b9) is still logging healthy 200 OK responses as of 15:02:34 — it started before/at the point the ConfigMap had bad content and its already-running nginx master process never reparsed the file. The new pod (revision 2, ReplicaSet frontend-d6db5d589) started fresh after the restart, read the current (broken) ConfigMap, and nginx failed its startup config validation. This explains both the crash loop AND why 2/2 old pods are still serving traffic fine — it's a stuck rolling update, not a full outage.

Let me check incident/blast-radius context to complete the picture.

Root Cause: CONFIRMED

Symptom actively occurring: kubectl get pods -n shop shows frontend-d6db5d589-dn4kr in CrashLoopBackOff, Restart Count 3, Last State Terminated/Error/Exit Code 1 (as of investigation time).

Mechanism (direct evidence):
``
kubectl logs frontend-d6db5d589-dn4kr -n shop --previous
2026/10/02 15:01:36 [emerg] 1#1: unknown directive "proxy_conect_timeout" in /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:9
nginx: [emerg] unknown directive "proxy_conect_timeout" in /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:9
`
The ConfigMap frontend-nginx (mounted at /etc/nginx/conf.d) contains a typo: proxy_conect_timeout instead of proxy_connect_timeout. This is baked into the ConfigMap's last-applied-configuration annotation, i.e., it was applied deliberately via kubectl apply, not a stray live edit. nginx validates its entire config at every container start and refuses to boot on an unknown directive — exit 1, repeat → CrashLoopBackOff.

Why only the new pod crashes, not all of them: The Deployment's live spec shows kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt: 2026-10-02T11:00:12-04:00 (15:00:12 UTC) on the pod template — a kubectl rollout restart was issued just 9 seconds after the ConfigMap/Deployment were created (15:00:03Z), spawning new ReplicaSet frontend-d6db5d589. The two pods in the old ReplicaSet frontend-76d98597b9 were already running (and had already loaded the config into the nginx master process in memory) and continued serving traffic fine — confirmed by their access logs showing continuous 200 OK responses through 15:02:34, well after the bad pod started crashing. New pods created after the ConfigMap went bad fail immediately on startup; already-running nginx processes don't reparse config without a reload.

Timing match: ConfigMap/typo exists now (resourceVersion 13224, newer than the Deployment's own 13235); rollout-restart annotation timestamp (15:00:12) lines up exactly with the new pod's creation and first crash at 15:00:53/15:01:36.

Current blast radius: Deployment shows READY 2/2, AVAILABLE 2, UP-TO-DATE 1/2 — the two old pods are still healthy and serving all traffic. This is a stuck rolling update, not a user-facing outage. get_incident/service_impact show no correlated alerts or downstream dependents affected.

Self-check
Alternative ruled out: not an OOM (no OOMKilled events, memory limit 64Mi not hit), not an image pull issue (image already present, pulled successfully 4x), not a readiness-probe-only issue (probe fails because the process never starts — container never binds to port 80).
Direct evidence of the reported symptom: CrashLoopBackOff state + exit code 1 + the exact nginx [emerg] parse error at container startup — this is the primary mechanism, not inferred.
Timing explained: config became invalid, then rollout restart created a fresh pod against the already-bad config at the exact timestamp matching first crash.

Remediation Validation

`text
VALIDATED FIXES:
FIX CONFIGMAP TYPO: kubectl patch configmap frontend-nginx -n shop --type merge -p \
   '{"data":{"default.conf":"upstream api {\n    server api:8080;\n}\nserver {\n    listen 80;\n    location /healthz { return 200 \"ok\\n\"; }\n    location /api/ {\n        proxy_pass http://api/;\n        proxy_connect_timeout 2s;\n    }\n    location / { return 200 \"shop frontend\\n\"; }\n}\n"}}'
   Validated by: kubectl get configmap frontend-nginx -n shop -o yaml → confirmed exact broken line 9 is
   "proxy_conect_timeout 2s;" inside the /api/ location block; corrected directive is "proxy_connect_timeout 2s;".
   Risk: low | Undo: kubectl patch configmap frontend-nginx -n shop --type merge -p '{"data":{"default.conf":"<prior content>"}}'
   Note: BLOCKED under current READ-ONLY/ASK policy (mutating kubectl denied). Requires an engineer with write access.
   Effect once applied: kubelet syncs the ConfigMap volume to the pod (~60s), and kubelet's existing CrashLoopBackOff
   restart cycle on frontend-d6db5d589-dn4kr will pick up the corrected config on its next retry — no further action needed.

ROLLBACK (NOT RECOMMENDED): kubectl rollout undo deployment/frontend -n shop
   Validated by: kubectl get replicaset -n shop -l app=frontend → confirmed revision-1 ReplicaSet
   frontend-76d98597b9 (2/2 ready) still exists, so a rollback target technically exists.
   Rejected because: the Deployment's pod template references the ConfigMap by name only — rolling back the
   Deployment revision does NOT revert the ConfigMap's data. The broken ConfigMap would persist and any future
   pod restart/reschedule of the "healthy" old pods would hit the same crash. This does not address root cause.
``

Recommended action: Fix #1 only — correct the ConfigMap directive typo. This is the sole fix in the causal chain.

incident.summary:
## Incident Report

**What Happened**

At 2026-10-02T15:01:03Z, a high-severity KubePodCrashLooping alert fired for the `shop` service. Investigation of the live cluster found pod `frontend-d6db5d589-dn4kr` (part of the Deployment `frontend`) in CrashLoopBackOff status with 3 restarts, last terminated with Exit Code 1 [4, 7]. The Deployment showed READY 2/2, AVAILABLE 2, UP-TO-DATE 1/2, indicating only the newest pod was affected while the Deployment overall remained healthy [5, 8].

**Root Cause**

The root cause was a syntax error in the `frontend-nginx` ConfigMap: the directive `proxy_conect_timeout` (missing the "n" in "connect") is invalid, causing nginx to fail config validation at startup with `unknown directive "proxy_conect_timeout" in /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf:9` [6, 9]. This typo is present in the ConfigMap's `last-applied-configuration` annotation, indicating it was introduced via a deliberate `kubectl apply` rather than a live edit [9]. A `kubectl rollout restart` was issued at 15:00:12 UTC, per the `kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt` annotation on the pod template, creating a new ReplicaSet (`frontend-d6db5d589`) whose pods read the already-broken ConfigMap on startup and failed immediately [7, 13]. The older ReplicaSet (`frontend-76d98597b9`) pods were already running prior to this and had the config loaded into their nginx master process in memory, so they never re-parsed the file and continued serving traffic normally, as shown by continuous 200 OK responses in their access logs [8, 12]. The timing of the restart annotation, pod creation, and first crash align closely, consistent with this causal chain [7, 13].

**Impact & Timeline**

This is a stuck rolling update rather than a full outage: the two old-revision pods remained healthy and serving all traffic (READY 2/2, AVAILABLE 2) while the single new-revision pod repeatedly crashed [5, 8, 12]. No correlated alerts or downstream service impact were identified [14, 15].

## Ruled Out
- OOM/memory limit exceeded — no OOMKilled events observed, and the container never reached a point to consume memory since it fails at config validation before binding to port 80 [6, 7].
- Image pull failure — the image `nginx:1.27-alpine` was already present and successfully used across both ReplicaSets [5, 8].
- Readiness/liveness probe misconfiguration as root cause — probe failures are a downstream symptom of the process never starting, not the underlying failure [6, 7].
- Stray/live ConfigMap edit — the typo is embedded in the `last-applied-configuration` annotation, showing it was applied intentionally via `kubectl apply`, not a manual live edit [9].
- Rollback as a fix — reverting the Deployment revision would not change the ConfigMap data, leaving the broken config in place for any future pod restart [8, 9].

## Not Checked
- Full rollout history (`kubectl rollout history`) — blocked by organizational policy on mutating kubectl operations [11].
- Prior ConfigMap revisions / diff of what exactly changed before the typo was introduced — not retrievable due to the same rollout-history restriction [11].
- Broader incident correlation beyond the `frontend`/`shop` service — `service_impact` and `get_incident` queries returned no downstream effects, but deeper dependency tracing was not performed [14, 15].
